jobs.title: Program Director Lodi California
jobs.description:
The rewards at Healogics are immense, starting with the important work we do to change patients’ lives. We also understand that meaningful work is hard work, and we are committed to supporting and compensating our employees for the tremendous service they provide.

Think you are a great fit? Learn more about this role here:

Healogics is the largest provider of advanced wound care services in the United States, treating more than 300,000 chronic wound patients annually across over 600 sites. With an aging society, obesity and diabetes on the rise, and an uptick in surgical procedures, the number of patients with non-healing wounds that would benefit from expert care is dramatically increasing. As a result, the company is working to provide our differentiated, quality outcomes to as many patients that would benefit through our out-patient clinic partnerships

The Program Director or Program Manager is responsible for the management and the strategic growth of the Wound Care Program for the assigned area of responsibility. This position is responsible for the complete oversight of the Wound Care Center, to include the following functions: day-to-day center operations, staff management, financial management, quality/performance improvement, and community education. The Program Director/Program Manager is also responsible for maintaining collaborative and consultative client relationships within and outside the hospital organization and for creating effective working relationships between Healogics and the hospital.

All Healogics employees must perform their job responsibilities according to all Healogics policies, Hospital policies, as well as to accrediting organizations, federal and state regulation, and to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) guidelines, as applicable.

Essential Functions/Responsibilities: (Percentage times shown in parenthesis next to each function)

Manages the Center’s Operations (20%):

Oversees the day-to-day management of outpatient clinic(s) and other wound continuum programs, as applicable.
Continuously assesses current clinic flows, processes and procedures, identifies areas of improvement, and develops and implements best practices and appropriate changes to improve outcomes, using the company’s resources.
Works with hospital and company personnel to ensure availability of adequate resources, supplies, equipment and services.
Facilitates the flow of information and maximizes effective communication throughout the program.
Prioritizes responsibilities and directs the work of the Center’s clinical staff and non- clinical staff.
Collaborates with other health care providers, Wound Care Center Providers, and Medical Director regarding clinic and patient needs.
Manages direct reports in conjunction with the company and hospital HR departments. This includes interviewing, hiring, motivating, coaching, counselling, establishing performance expectations, and conducting performance reviews. (5%)

Performs Financial Management (10%)

Manages and coordinates all aspects of the revenue cycle for Healogics and for the hospital partner, as appropriate.
Stays current with reimbursement changes, providing physician and staff updates and education as needed.
Reviews key financial reports, identifies key indicator trends and develops plans to implement best practices to ensure fiscal responsibility.
Tracks and reports all ancillary revenues generated by the program.
Manages costs through appropriate utilization and management of labor and supply.
Works with Healogics support team to complete financial reviews and presents results to hospital leadership.

Manages Community Education/Marketing functions (40%)

Works directly with the hospital and Healogics marketing departments to ensure that the wound care program has established strategic marketing plans and works with the same group and the hospital physician liaison to plan, coordinate, and execute activities directed toward increasing patient referrals to the wound care center(s).
Works collaboratively, as part of a multi-functional team, to best determine key target referral sources, and develops a systematic approach to build those customer relationships and increase wound care center referrals.
Maintains, monitors and updates the list of Physician Practice(s) within a given radius of the hospital on an ongoing basis.
Visits Physician Practices and interacts with key physicians to provide awareness of the Wound Care Center program, using educational marketing materials. Also documents all physician office interactions, as well as the visits with the Physician Practices in the Healogics Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system.
Communicates on a regular basis with the (C)DO and/or (C)VPO and the hospital executive sponsor regarding goals, targets, and other relevant referral development information, as needed.

Manages Quality/Performance Improvement functions (10%)

Implements and manages a continuous Wound Care Center Performance Improvement Program (PIP) and strives to meet Wound Care Center quality indicators. Ensures program is integrated into the partner hospital’s PIP program.
Participates in hospital committees as appropriate and ensures timely and accurate documentation in the patient record and outcomes database.
Monitors patient, referring physician and customer satisfaction.
Ensures that Patient Safety Guidelines are followed, that Healogics employees complete annual compliance requirements, and creates an environment that promotes the escalation of compliance concerns as appropriate.

Manages Relationships (15%)

Maintains excellent relationship with hospital client and continuously seeks to understand needs, confirm goal alignment and demonstrate value proposition. Identifies the hospital strategic goals and objectives and manages the program to achieve those goals, while remaining compliant with all Healogics operations standards. Works effectively and seamlessly at all levels within the partner hospital. Participates in hospital department/management meetings and actively participates in Hospital communication activities.
Builds and develops effective working relationships with panel physicians, clinical and support staff. Encourages all program staff to provide excellent customer service to members of other hospital departments.
Meets regularly with leadership including hospital and area management.
Performs other duties as required.

Required Education, Experience And Credentials

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Nursing or related field preferred and 1 year of marketing/community education in the healthcare industry or clinical operations experience
OR Associate’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Nursing or related field preferred and 2 or more years of marketing/community education in the healthcare industry or clinical operations experience
OR High School Diploma and 4 years or more years of marketing/community education in the healthcare industry or clinical operations experience
Management experience preferred

Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint)

Strong organization, time management skills and ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment

Ability to work with Healogics and hospital management.

Improve Your Tomorrow (IYT) is seeking a strategic, relationship-driven Director of Development

for someone who can build relationships, identify opportunities, secure funding, and drive revenue while working closely with the Regional Executive Director and IYT’s national Shared Services Development team.

—from prospecting and fund development planning to grant writing, donor cultivation, sponsorships, events, stewardship, and Salesforce management.

Develop and execute an annual fundraising plan with clear revenue targets.

Provide revenue forecasts, scenario models, and progress-to-goal reports.

🔹 Drive Grant Revenue

.

Lead sponsorship development and revenue generation for regional events.

jobs.description:
Company Description

The San Francisco Adult Probation Department values the individuality and diversity of justice involved adults, recognize the unique challenges they face, and invest in their success through services designed to help them permanently exit the criminal justice system. Our reentry and rehabilitative services complement our supervision strategies by providing a unique blend of opportunity and accountability. We extend a continuum of integrated services to address our client’s criminogenic needs and empower them to become productive members of the community. SFAPD dedicates endless energy toward enhancing public safety, seeking victim restoration and accountability, providing structured and evidence-based supervision, all on the behalf of the Superior Court of San Francisco.

Job Description

Reporting to the Department Head, Deputy Directors function at the highest level of department management and are responsible for all functions and activities of a major division or area. Positions in this class are exempt from Civil Service appointment (Charter Section 10.104); appointment to Deputy Director positions are made by the department head and appointees serve at their discretion.

Under general direction of the Chief Adult Probation Officer of the Adult Probation Department (ADP), the Deputy Director of Finance and Administrative Services is senior executive -level manager that plans, develops and implements all fiscal and administrative functions and activities of the department.

Positions in this class provide executive direction for highly specialized professional functions within departments. Incumbents in these positions make decisions critically impacting diverse functions of the division/bureau; manage organizational changes; and provide direction to Division Managers responsible for major program areas.

Deputy Directors within a single department may be allocated at different classification levels, including acting on behalf of the Chief Adult Probation Officer

This position oversees the financial, budgetary, procurement, fiscal and administrative affairs of the Adult Probation Department. The incumbent advises the Chief Adult Probation Officer on financial and budgetary issues, operations, human resources planning and administrative policy and legislative matters. The primary functions of this position are as follows:

Department Accounting Manager
Serve as subject matter expert overseeing accounting and budgeting structures and hierarchies, and developing and maintaining related policies and procedures
Provide leadership, coordination, and primary point of contact for internal and external auditors; developing, composing, and implementing corrective action plans, progress reporting, and practice change across the department.
Lead development and implementation of internal controls to ensure fiduciary integrity and compliance with city/county, state, and federal fiscal, accounting, budgeting, contracting and purchasing policies and procedures and regulatory requirements.

Chief Budget Strategist:
Develop and coordinate budget development processes and strategies to maximize funding streams from state, federal, sales, tax, vehicles, and grants.
Develop and manage the department’s master budget production schedule, convening division budget meetings to develop budget recommendations;
Compile and consolidate annual budget recommendations, appropriation modifications and mid-cycle budget amendments, and revenue and expense cost impact analysis;
Oversee position control and reconciliation; and managing budget expenditure and revenue projections, reporting, and budgetary controls.
Plan, develop and present budget narratives, budget policies and procedures, and ensuring budget system integrity and reconciliation, and budget variance reporting.

Procurement
Serve as subject matter expert overseeing all procurement including request for proposal and other solicitation, personal service contract(PSC) development, establishing procurement policies and procedures.

Interpret and ensure compliance with city procurement regulations
Oversee financial integrity and reconciliation of financial, accounting, budgeting, banking, and contracting systems
Develop and producing financial and statistical reporting of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial projections
Account reconciliations, discrepancy resolutions, cashiering and escheatment functions, and adjusting accounting transactions and write-offs.
Plan, develop, and implement financial business analytics and dashboard reporting system solution to integrate financial data in disparate accounting, banking, and case management systems.
Develop and implement financial and statistical feasibility studies for compliance reporting, legislative impact and funding analysis, new operations and program proposals, grant proposals, capital projects and facility renovations and relocations.

Human Resources
Manage and oversee all areas of human resources including leave management, reasonable accommodations, examination development and administration, recruitment, labor and employee relations, payroll and operations.
Manage and coordinate the development and review of departmental personnel policies and procedures.
Interpret and ensure compliance with CSC Rules, City Charter, Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs), and other employment laws and regulations.
Oversee the day-to-day responsibilities of the ADA reasonable accommodation and leave management programs as well as Workers’ Compensation claims.
Develop and provide training to managers on employee/labor issues and trends, including administration and facilitation of disciplinary and grievance processes and performance management
Advise managers and supervisors on employee/labor relations issues, CBA interpretation, disciplinary actions, grievances, employee coaching, counseling, performance management, employment laws, CSC rules, City Charter, City and County of San Francisco (CCSF) policies, Department policies.

Compliance
Monitor, analyze, and interpret federal, state and local legislation and regulations;
Conduct full internal affairs investigations
Serve as department audit manager coordinating responses to local, state and federal audits.
Develop and implement strategies and administrative, personnel, financial and operations policies and procedures to achieve compliance;
Develop recommendations to minimize department financial and programmatic impacts.
Consult with department executives, directors, managers and staff to plan and develop new and updated administrative/management policies and procedures.
Consult with department executives, directors, managers and staff to plan, develop, and implement Department’s strategic plans including a Racial Equity, Five-Year Plans, etc.

Supervision
Planning, organizing, and managing day-to-day operations of the Finance and Administrative Services of the Department including subordinate work assignments and work schedules to ensure continuity of services to the general public and clients;
Supervise and train staff, evaluate their performance and takes or recommends appropriate action where disciplinary matters are concerned.

Department Representation
Developing and maintaining collaboratively works with other City departments, Superior Court, and other organizations on joint funding projects including inter-agency agreements, MOUs, grant agreements, contracts, and oversees integrity of financial, accounting, and budgeting operations.
Representing the department for budgeting, accounting, and financial related matters with City and County agencies, state and federal agencies and committees, and other organizations including the Mayor’s Budget Office, Board of Supervisors, other county, state, and federal agencies, and the public.
Developing and maintaining relationships with elected and appointed officials, state and federal representatives, community groups, and labor organizations.

Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Possession of a baccalaureate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, public administration, or a closely related field; AND

Three (3) years of progressively responsible managerial experience directing a complex financial and administrative operation, all of which must include supervisory experience.

Education Substitution:
Additional years of experience as listed above may substitute up to two years of the required degree (on a year for year basis).

Additional Information

The City and County of San Francisco encourages women, minorities and persons with disabilities to apply. Applicants will be considered regardless of their sex, race, age, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition (associated with cancer, a history of cancer, or genetic characteristics), HIV/AIDS status, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, military and veteran status, or other protected category under the law.

jobs.title: Executive Director, New York at OneGoal
jobs.description:
OneGoal transforms postsecondary advising and support so that every student can define their own future. Together with our partners, we're building a movement to close the opportunity gap. We work side-by-side with partner schools and districts to build their knowledge and capacity.

About The Organization

OneGoal transforms postsecondary advising and support so that every student can define their own future. Together with our partners, we're building a movement to close the opportunity gap. We work side-by-side with partner schools and districts to build their knowledge and capacity, leveraging existing resources and deep relationships within the school community to deliver effective, sustainable support for all students. The result is more effective support for all students. Our unique approach, honed over 15 years, prioritizes strong human relationships. And it's proven to deliver real student impact: An independent study by the University of Chicago found that OneGoal students are about 40% more likely to earn their postsecondary degrees than students from similar backgrounds.

Guided by a clear set of core values and beliefs, you will join an impressive group of staff across the country who believe in the untapped potential within students. The OneGoal team challenges themselves and others to regularly ask, "Is there a better way?" We believe that in order to create the change we seek, each person we hire brings a remarkable and diverse set of experiences, skills and characteristics that individually and collectively, will contribute to the radical change needed to move us towards a more just nation.

OneGoal in New York

Established in 2014, OneGoal New York works across high schools and districts to close the degree divide and expand postsecondary opportunities for young people. As the largest school district in the country, New York City serves 1.1 million students—including over 300,000 high schoolers across more than 400 high schools. Yet the disparity in college completion remains vast: only 24% of Black and Latinx 9th graders attain an associate or bachelor's degree within six years of high school graduation. This divide is not due to a lack of ambition or talent, but a lack of systemic support. OneGoal New York is changing that trajectory across the five boroughs and beyond, partnering with 18 high schools and postsecondary institutions to serve over 2,350 students this year. The results speak for themselves: 87% of OneGoal New York high school graduates enroll in a postsecondary institution, and 76% persist into their second year. At OneGoal, you'll be immersed in a culture of collaboration, shared purpose, and collective impact. Operating as part of a single 501(c)(3) national structure, our regional team directly implements high-impact programming while driving key fundraising, state advocacy, and growth initiatives across the region.

About The Role

What You'll Do

As the Executive Director (ED), New York, you enter OneGoal at a pivotal inflection point to serve as the region's primary external face, visionary leader, and chief revenue strategist. Reporting to the Chief Regional Operations Officer and sitting on OneGoal's national Leadership Group, you will support the authoring of the region's vision within OneGoal's org-wide 2030 Strategic Plan, crafting a compelling narrative that inspires internal and external stakeholders to invest in what is possible for young people.

Externally, you will champion our brand and call the plays on funder strategy to meet an ambitious $2.2M regional target, cultivating major donor relationships and expanding our footprint across New York City and New York State. Internally, you will serve as a steady, unifying leader who builds trust, strengthens organizational culture, and drives programmatic excellence. Ultimately, you will ensure long-term regional health, program excellence, and deep staff engagement.

Key Responsibilities

Are you an entrepreneurial leader ready to create the newest Hillel in North America? As the inaugural Executive Director of Hillel at Clemson University
, you will be the driving force behind creating a dynamic home for Jewish life that inspires students to explore and experience a vibrant Jewish community on campus. Utilizing an innovative approach and a go-getter attitude, you will craft the vision and build the strategy for engaging all Jewish students, establish a strong campus and community presence, develop key resources, and strengthen vital ties between Hillel, the University, and the local community. You will excel in this pivotal role if you are a builder with a start-up mindset who loves launching organizations from the ground up —setting long-term strategic vision, securing financial sustainability, and empowering students to take genuine ownership of Jewish life.
What you’ll do:

Strategy & Vision

Create a strategic vision in year one and lead the drive for a long-term plan for Hillel at Clemson.
Establish the necessary infrastructure for Hillel at Clemson to become a self-sustaining and top-notch nonprofit organization.

Fundraising & Financial Management

Exhibit leadership around financial resource development and cultivate the stakeholders who will help you get there, including lay leaders, Clemson community members, and local agencies.
Develop Hillel’s financial resources to establish financial sustainability in accordance with the size of the Jewish community and the needs of the strategic plan.
Develop policies and procedures that ensure sound financial practice and financial independence.
Identify, secure, and outfit appropriate rental space to be utilized for Hillel’s needs.

Stakeholder & External Relations

As the primary Hillel professional for Clemson, understand the unique culture of campus and find opportunities for partnership and connection where they intersect with Hillel’s priorities.
Work with University partners, Jewish community partners, and key stakeholders to educate and advocate for the needs and interests of Jewish college students in today’s world.
Connect Hillel at Clemson to the International Hillel movement and other national initiatives and programs.

Student Engagement

Inspire and organize pluralistic, diverse Jewish life on campus, creating strategies to expand the base of the Jewish student community to include a multiplicity of Jewish backgrounds and interests.
Act as a leader and convener of the community every day, during times of celebration and during times of challenge.
Serve as a trusted mentor and advisor to student leaders, empowering them to design and lead programming that reflects their own passions, build their leadership skills, and take genuine ownership of Jewish life on campus.

What You’ll Bring:

Professional Experience: 5+ years of professional work experience, including a proven track record in fundraising. Experience in management roles in the Jewish or secular nonprofit, higher education, or mission-driven organization world is a plus.
Education: Bachelor’s degree required, Master’s degree preferred. We will consider a range of candidates’ experiences and credentials.
Fundraising Prowess: Demonstrated success with financial resource development, including executing annual fundraising campaigns, cultivation, stewardship, and major gift solicitation through in-person, print, and online channels, as well as fiscal budgeting and financial forecasting.
Entrepreneurial Spirit: A strong entrepreneurial spirit and passion for building an organization from the ground up, paired with creative problem-solving and the attention to detail to create and follow through with a complex plan.
Strategic Execution: A track record of developing a strategic plan for an organization and executing it, along with building student engagement and leadership development programs and opportunities.
Relationship Focus: Strong relationship-building skills, comfort working with diverse populations, and an attitude of proactive communication and collaboration across offices and agencies.
Storytelling & Presence: Robust storytelling skills to engage others in support of a new endeavor, with an inspiring presence that helps others deepen their interest in Jewish life and creates space for a diversity of perspectives so all student voices are heard.
Jewish Literacy: Expertise in leading complex conversations about Judaism and Israel in a way that is approachable and meets students at various points in their personal Jewish journey, with a gift for inspiring interest in pluralistic, diverse Jewish life.

What you’ll receive:

Salary: $85,000 – $100,000, depending upon skills, qualifications, and experience.
Comprehensive Benefits: A comprehensive benefits package and generous paid time off.
Professional Growth: Paid opportunities for professional development, peer engagement, mentoring, and skill-building, including global conferences for personal and professional development throughout the U.S. and Israel.
Mentorship & Support: Mentorship by a fellow Hillel Director and strategic support from a dedicated Campus Support Director at Hillel’s Schusterman International Center.
Lay Leadership: A supportive and committed board of lay leaders and faculty.
Relocation: Assistance is available.

A Brief Introduction to Hillel at Clemson:

Hillel at Clemson will serve more than 500 Jewish undergraduate and graduate students at Clemson University in Clemson, SC. Hillel will be part of a Clemson campus community that furthers civic engagement and innovation, practices collaboration and partnership, and values diversity, equity, and inclusion. Hillel at Clemson is affiliated with Hillel International, which enriches the lives of Jewish students so they may enrich the Jewish people and the world, and envisions a world where every student is inspired to make an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel.

About Clemson University

Clemson University is an R-1 public research institution consistently recognized for student success and community engagement. In the U.S. News & World Report 2026 rankings, Clemson was named the top national and public university in South Carolina and ranked No. 36 among all public universities nationwide. With an acceptance rate around 33%, Clemson’s out-of-state footprint has grown significantly in the past decade, aided by its flagship honors college, which is ranked fourth in the nation. A land grant university, Clemson’s student body has diverse interests and socio-economic backgrounds. Clemson’s exceptionally strong athletic programs are a pillar of its intense sense of campus community and unity, bringing top student-athletes from across the country and the world into its student body. Clemson is one of very few universities to receive an A+ rating for its work to curb antisemitism and create an open environment for Jewish students to thrive.

About Clemson And Upstate South Carolina

Nestled in the scenic Upstate of South Carolina and on the shore of Lake Hartwell, the town of Clemson offers a unique blend of small-town charm and surrounding natural beauty. It has an energetic and welcoming atmosphere, with a lively main street and a steady flow of cultural and athletic events. The surrounding Upstate region is known for its rolling foothills and easy access to outdoor recreation, including hiking, boating, and a short distance to the Blue Ridge Mountains, which can be seen from campus.

Although the town of Clemson is small, it is only 40 minutes from Greenville, ranked by U.S. News & World Report as the #4 city in the United States to live in and the #3 top small city by Condé Nast Readers’ Choice Awards. Greenville offers vibrant Jewish life, myriad cultural activities, and some of the most exciting employment opportunities in the Sun Belt.

Don’t check off all the boxes or meet every single requirement? We have learned that potential candidates hesitate to apply for a job unless they meet every requirement. Hillel is dedicated to inclusivity and to valuing diversity and equity in the workplace. If this opportunity excites you but your background may not be a perfect match, we still encourage you to apply.

If you have any questions about this role, please contact Jennifer Sosnow, Director of Executive Talent, Hillel International, at jsosnow@hillel.org

About Hillel International

In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Director of Operations serves as the senior operational leader responsible for the day-to-day performance of Columbus Aesthetic & Plastic Surgery across all locations and service lines.

The Managing Director will be accountable for the overall leadership, architecture, implementation, usage, and roadmap of a portfolio of enterprise systems, enhancing and maintaining these systems to ensure they effectively support the Federation’s expansive fundraising and business operations.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Strategy:

Partner with the CIO to provide leadership, coordination, change enablement, and delivery oversight of the systems roadmap and strategy.
Collaborate with business partners across the organization including Finance, Development, Marketing, Donor Services, and HR to understand and prioritize their needs, and develop strategies that meet business objectives.

Partner with vendors and project management resources to manage scope, schedule, and resources allocation to ensure work is delivered in accordance with business needs.
Establish and lead governance processes for enterprise applications, including prioritization, roadmap planning, change control, architecture reviews, and investment decisions.

Direct the strategy, architecture, implementation, support, enhancement, and lifecycle management of the Federation's enterprise application ecosystem, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and technology strategy.
Oversee the roadmap and release schedules for all systems and ensure a strong change management process.
Ensure a cohesive enterprise architecture through effective integration of systems, data platforms, and third-party applications.
Lead master data management and governance initiatives and ensure ongoing data quality controls and processes are in place.
Manage partner relationships to ensure quality service delivery including agreements, renewals, and procurement.
Lead and initiate technology change throughout the organization; evangelize the use of technology and spearhead education and training opportunities for staff.

Department Leadership:

Lead and enable a multidisciplinary team of managers, analysts, architects, administrators, developers, and support personnel responsible for the Federation's enterprise application portfolio. Establish a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, operational excellence, and customer service while developing future technology leaders.
Assist in recruiting, mentoring, and maximizing the growth potential of a high-performing IT team, including goalsetting, performance management, and continuous skills development.
Assist with establishing and implementing policies and procedures that achieve the directives and strategies of the CIO, President, Senior Leadership Team, and Board of Trustees.
Function as a strong contributor to the IT and Federation management team, acting as a proxy for the CIO in departmental or technology decisions.
Develop strong working relationships with the members of the lay leader committee and external advisors.
Perform other duties assigned to meet the goals and objectives of the IT department and the Federation.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in technology management roles.

Demonstrated experience leading large-scale enterprise systems, upgrades, migrations, consolidations, and business process improvement initiatives involving ERP, CRM, HRIS, marketing, and data platforms.

Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to influence a diverse group of stakeholders and drive change at an organizational level.
Ability to work independently, prioritize and engage in a variety of tasks simultaneously while consistently meeting short deadline situations.
High attention to detail, follow-up, self-motivated, proactive, and solution minded.
Experience with Oracle NetSuite and Salesforce strongly preferred.
Experience with Microsoft cloud solutions, Data Warehousing, Business Process Automation, AI, a plus.

ABOUT THE FEDERATION

Chief Executive Officer

Nursetech Medical Corp
| Remote (US), up to 20% travel | Full-time, Open to Part-time to start

Reports to the Board. Works alongside the founder/CTO and sales team.

Nurses lose hours a shift, and hospitals lose millions of dollars, to seemingly-small that actually have real consequences for patients. Our mission at Nursetech Medical is to build devices that nurses trust, for the patients they protect.

Our flagship product, the Cordflex Clip, is a patented single- device that’s FDA listed with an established quality system, generating early revenue, and selling through a nationally distributing sales team. We are selling to and trialing at various major hospital systems, but looking to significantly expand from early growth mode. We recently closed the first tranche of our seed round and are raising the remainder now.
We are hiring a CEO to close our seed round and scale a product hospitals are already buying. You will be tasked to focus 100% initially on the raise, then transition to fully own and direct the growth of our current infrastructure. This is a unique opportunity to demonstrate how your business acumen can guide a fast-growing business to significant growth in a transformative and impactful field.

What you'll do

Own the raise end to end: pipeline, pitch, diligence, close. The founder/CTO supports technical diligence and materials.
Serve as the public face of the company with health systems, partners, and at trade shows and conferences.
Direct marketing and sales strategy and execution
Identify new markets and set the timing for expansion
Hire, build repeatable processes, test fast, cut what fails
Report metrics to investors and the Board
Ensure the team upholds FDA, quality system, and corporate governance compliance

Your first year

Seed round closed
Multiple health systems converted from evaluation to signed, system-wide contracts
Revenue grown several times over, with the unit economics to reach profitability
Sales team expanded and producing against clear, measured targets
Repeatable playbooks in place for VAC approval, distributor onboarding, and system rollout
Product roadmap beyond Cordflex validated and funded

Qualifications

5+ years in medical devices, healthcare technology, or a comparable regulated industry, including 2+ in a senior leadership role.
Track record raising capital
Degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, or related field; an advanced degree (MBA or equivalent) is preferred. A degree is not a substitute for operating experience.
Proficiency in Finance and Business Planning, including budgeting, forecasting, and managing resources to support sustainable growth.
Experience in Operations Management, with a track record of optimizing processes, overseeing product delivery, and supporting organizational scalability.
Demonstrated capability in Sales, particularly in B2B or healthcare-related environments, with experience building and managing strategic partnerships.
Strong Strategic Planning skills, including setting long-term vision, defining priorities, and executing roadmaps for market expansion and product development.
Ability to collaborate effectively with clinical stakeholders, investors, and cross-functional teams; strong communication and negotiation skills.
Understanding of healthcare delivery environments and relevant regulatory considerations; experience with hospital or clinical procurement processes is beneficial.
Authorized to work in the US

Strongly preferred

RN or former RN, ideally critical care background
An active clinical and hospital network you can bring with you: nurse leaders, VAC members, supply chain, or system executives
Marketing and brand-building experience
Product development, market research, or focus group experience
Existing investor relationships in MedTech or healthcare

Compensation

Equity-only until seed round is closed. Meaningful equity, negotiable based on experience. Salary scales to a base of $110,000 to $120,000 at close, depending on experience.

Who thrives here

Someone hungry. A shrewd, deliberate, and quick action taker. Comfortable wearing many hats and effective at helping others wear them too. Someone with a deep passion for the medical world, helping patients, clinicians, and hospitals alike.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director, Market Impact (Remote in Milwaukee, WI)
new_jobs.description:
March of Dimes leads the fight for the health of all moms and babies. We are advocating for policies to protect them. We are working to radically improve the health care they receive. We are pioneering research to find solutions. We are empowering families with programs, knowledge and tools to have healthier pregnancies. By uniting communities, we are building a brighter future for us all.
We are dedicated to hiring a diverse workforce that fosters opportunities for personal and professional development. We provide a collaborative and supportive environment built upon our fundamental core principles where each employee is valued. Join us in the fight for healthy moms and strong babies.
SCOPE: 

The Executive Director of Market Impact serves as the Market leader providing overall management, planning, execution, and leadership for all aspects of a designated market. This includes creating mission impact, mobilizing supporters, growing a diversified revenue portfolio, donor stewardship, board/staff development and maintaining overall budgets. The Executive Director will also maintain a donor portfolio.
The Executive Director of Market Impact is responsible for providing management, planning, execution and leadership for all aspects of the organization. This includes creating mission impact, mobilizing supporters, growing a diversified revenue portfolio, donor stewardship, board/staff development, human resource management, and maintaining overall budgets.
The Executive Director of Market Impact is responsible for positioning March of Dimes as a leader in maternal and child health care in his/her respective market as well as establishing effective partnerships and collaborations with corporations, foundations, community/corporate leaders, government officials, other community organizations/nonprofits and supporters.
The Executive Director reports to the Associate Vice President of Market Impact sharing successes, problem solving and providing a supportive network for the Market Impact team. This role leads and develops a combination of local donor relationship, mission and enterprise shared services staff to drive results.
RESPONSIBILITIES
:

Mission Leadership and Impact 

Lead, develop and implement a results-based local strategic planning process that:
Places Mission Impact at the forefront of all work.
Advances maternal and infant health equity, identifies measurable strategies and solutions that address community mission needs, and contributes to diversified revenue growth.
Translate mission and advocacy in a manner that demonstrates impact; identifying supporter philanthropic interest.
Leverages Mission Impact Opportunities to engage supporters and drives expansion/implementation of mission programs, in a manner that achieves revenue growth and measurable mission impact strategies.
Demonstrate adaptive leadership in a manner that establishes March of Dimes as a recognized and valued leader in maternal and infant healthcare.
Identify, recruit, and retain influential state level volunteer leaders and coach them to propel Mission Impact priorities.
Lead Mission Impact staff ensuring they collaborate with fundraising staff and volunteers; providing Mission Impact education that demonstrates how to use data to drive mission deliverables, advocacy initiatives, and revenue growth.
Responsible for creating a revenue pipeline and funding to provide ongoing support for both new and existing mission initiatives (i.e. NFS, SPC, etc.).

Diversified Revenue Portfolio

Lead, develop and implement a results-based local strategic planning process that places emphasis on a diversified revenue portfolio by:
Ensuring each market employee maintains and grows a donor revenue portfolio by carrying-out developing donor relationship principles, identifying philanthropic interests, and moving donors through the donor continuum in a manner that retains existing donors and increases donor giving.
Ensuring each applicable market employee develops, maintains and manages a pipeline of qualified individual gift donors with concentration in major gifts and planned-giving.
Ensuring each applicable market employee achieves corporate engagement revenue goals in a manner that increases local revenue by identifying appropriate corporate partners and developing alliances that accelerate the development of strategic partnerships that drive March of Dimes mission impact and mobilizes supporters.
Ensures each applicable market employee achieves Mission Investment Opportunities product revenue goal achievement.
Develop, maintain, and grow individual donor portfolio in a manner that contributes to diversified revenue growth in individual giving, major gifts, corporate engagement, and Mission Investment Opportunities.
Collaborate with national business partners to leverage local relationships that have potential to elevate to national partnerships.
Ensure CRM data integrity by setting goals and expectations, monitoring use and utilizing data and reporting to further business.
Remain current on donor needs, market trends, and competitor actions in order to create reliable revenue forecasts and to identify opportunities for donor development locally.

Strategic Planning and Budgeting

Develops a comprehensive, results-based strategic plan that incorporates impact, movement, growth and performance.
Ensuring execution of the local strategic plan in a manner that results in proven impact and exceeds market targets for productivity and profitability.
Develops revenue projections and provides financial analysis.
Oversee the development of budgets in a manner in which the market shows an increase in net profitability and productivity according to national standards.
Review and manage strategic plan with staff on an ongoing basis with a minimum of a quarterly market review.
Ensure market staff fully comprehend strategic plan and strategies they are responsible for executing to achieve success.

Volunteer Leadership

Lead, develop and implement a results-based local strategic planning process that identifies, engages, and maintains influential volunteer leaders and board members to drive impact and secure revenue.
Build a pipeline to constantly recruit new high-level volunteer leaders and board members.
Ensure ongoing training and orientation of all volunteers in the market that aligns with the local and national strategic plan.
Collaborate with Volunteer Leadership Development to ensure implementation of market board excellence and the use of market board excellence tools/resources (i.e. including standards of excellence with fundraising committees).
Recruit, activate and retain influential, financially strong, diverse volunteer leadership and market board members resulting in revenue growth and market impact.
Ensure volunteer leaders are engaged in a way that builds a community of mission advocates.

Staff Development

Hire and develop a diverse market staff that demonstrate passion for our mission and have the expected skills, fit and proven success to exceed expected goals and results.
Establish and discuss individual goals and accountabilities for performance and behavior (at the beginning of the year) that align with organizational goals and include benchmarks and measurable milestones.
Hold staff accountable to market and individual net productivity and profitability goals by utilizing reports and measurement tools and provide staff with constructive feedback that leads to improved performance on a consistent basis (at minimum quarterly, at best weekly).
Provide coaching and professional development in a manner that results in skill and behavioral development and results in staff retention and career pathing.
Accountable to writing and delivering annual performance reviews in a timely manner that align with the expected HR standards.
Create a productive, professional, respectful and culturally diverse work environment where all staff can be the best version of themselves.

QUALIFICATIONS:

4 year college degree or equivalent experience. 
Experience in managing multiple staff over various functional areas, including employees who telecommute.
Experience in a nonprofit environment a plus.
Detail-oriented with strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong leadership/management skills with the ability to motivate staff and lead change.
Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills.
Proven track record building internal and external relationships.

The Director of Operations and Programs is the Executive Director’s most senior internal leader and trusted thought partner, bringing the Executive Director's vision to life inside the New Art Center - a beloved, nearly 50-year-old community arts organization - with real agency to shape how programs, people, and operations come together.

Position Summary

Reporting directly to the Executive Director, the Director of Operations and Programs leads all operational and programmatic functions at the New Art Center. This is the organization's number-two role, with the primary responsibilities of managing teams and turning strategy into strong internal execution. The Director of Operations and Programs oversees the Programs Teams to deliver exceptional educational offerings, holding them accountable for program quality, student retention, and ambitious earned-revenue goals. Personal fluency in curriculum and pedagogy is a real asset but not a prerequisite - what matters most is knowing how to identify, hire, and manage the talent who has that expertise, while running a well-organized, efficient internal operation.

The Director of Operations and Programs is responsible for ensuring operational excellence in the daily functions of the New Art Center. This means establishing excellent communications with students, families, faculty, and staff to optimize visitor experience and support robust enrollment; managing internal financial controls and reporting; overseeing building maintenance and safety; and facilitating consistent, reliable administrative systems across the organization.

The Director of Operations and Programs will work in close partnership with the Executive Director. We're looking for a strategic, detail-oriented leader who is achievement-driven, resilient, and brings a positive, can-do attitude to everything they do. The Director of Operations and Programs must have a strong management track record, holding teams to high standards while remaining warm, motivated, and invested in their growth.

Key Responsibilities

1. Operations, Systems & Infrastructure

Oversee daily operations, systems, and administrative workflows - registration, scheduling, the Art Center Canvas CRM, and reporting - for efficient, student-centered service.
Support the Executive Director in the annual budget process and expense management - monitoring expenses and income against the annual budget, running audits, and proactively eliminating waste and unnecessary spend; participate as needed in the annual external audit.
Serve as the internal HR lead: hire, supervise, and support all staff and contractors (recruitment, hiring, onboarding, performance management), partnering with an external HR consultant or Board representative as needed.
Oversee the administration of payroll and benefits, and monitor compliance of employment practices, including employee handbooks, performance reviews, and personnel record-keeping.
Responsible for the 24/7 security, safety, maintenance, cleanliness, and timely repair of the building.
Manage space rentals, daily building operations, and relations with service suppliers and contractors.
Establish and ensure compliance with all organizational policies and operational best practices.

2. Educational Programs, Curriculum & Earned Revenue Growth

Oversee all visual arts education programs (adults, teens, youth, camps, workshops), managing the Programs Teams to build strong curricular pathways and to drive earned-revenue growth through enrollment, pricing, and retention strategy - with accountability for program quality and results.
In collaboration with the Operations Coordinator, grow revenue from space rentals, events, and membership programs, and help identify alternate streams of earned revenue beyond core programming.
Collaborate with marketing professionals to promote programs, strengthen enrollment, and raise the New Art Center's visibility in the community.
Recruit and develop faculty, and improve student retention and loyalty through program quality, pathway clarity, and community-building.
Diversify faculty and student populations through targeted recruitment.
Champion new, unconventional approaches to programming and engagement, particularly where there are opportunities to strengthen participation, relevance, and revenue. 

3. Partnership with the Executive Director

Serve as the Executive Director's most trusted internal advisor, translating the Executive Director's vision and strategy into concrete plans, staff direction, and day-to-day execution.
Partner with the Executive Director on the FY27 annual plan and long-term program strategy.
Support the Executive Director with reporting to the Board of Governors on programs, operations, and financial sustainability, and collaborate directly with the relevant Board of Governors committees needed.
Bring forward ideas and recommendations candidly, exercise sound independent judgment, and partner closely with the Executive Director - recognizing that final direction and organizational decisions rest with the Executive Director. 
Communicate the Executive Director's priorities to staff clearly and consistently.

4. Team Leadership

Set a high bar for team performance and accountability, while providing genuine mentorship, warmth, and investment in each person's development.
Model consistent follow-through and attention to detail, and build a culture of accountability, ownership, and improvement.
Provide the steady leadership and motivational presence that keeps the team focused, energized, and driving toward ambitious goals.

What We're Looking For

8–10+ years of progressive management experience in operations, programs, or finance, ideally within an arts, education, or mission-driven nonprofit organization. Bachelor's degree required; an advanced degree in arts administration, nonprofit management, or a related field is preferred.
Strong command of how to evaluate program and curriculum quality and hold managers accountable to it - knowing how to identify, hire, and manage the talent that has that expertise; personal fluency in pedagogy is a plus.
A collaborator with executive presence to lead staff, faculty, and cross-functional teams.
A track record of driving and exceeding ambitious revenue or performance targets, with strong financial acumen and an entrepreneurial, outside-the-box mindset.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, resourceful, and relentlessly focused on execution and results. 
A direct, clear communicator and natural collaborator who welcomes feedback and coaching, and follows through on implementation.
The judgment to operate as a strong second-in-command - collaborative, trustworthy, discreet, and able to build confidence across staff, faculty, Board members, and community partners. 
Strong working knowledge of finance systems and experience with CRM/registration systems, budgeting tools, and data-driven decision-making.
A genuine passion for community arts, nonprofit work, and mission-driven impact, with a commitment to equity-centered programming. Experience with a nonprofit Board of Directors/Governors and/or Newton community is a plus.

We recognize that great candidates don't always meet every qualification. If you're excited about this role and believe you could contribute meaningfully to the team at New Art, we encourage you to apply.

What We Offer

Salary range: $85,000–$100,000, based on experience, including a $5,000 discretionary wellness, professional development, or health care stipend.
Generous paid time off, including full compensation during closure between Christmas and New Year's.
Complimentary New Art Center classes.
A collaborative, mission-driven team environment.
The opportunity to directly deliver on mission - strengthening arts education and community impact through the programs and operations you lead.
The chance to build and elevate the New Art Center's programs and operations while mentoring the next generation of nonprofit and arts professionals.
The opportunity to help shape the future of a beloved, nearly 50-year-old community arts organization - recently named one of the top 5 places to discover (or rediscover) creativity by Boston Magazine.

You will keep New Art operating efficiently from the inside. The Executive Director will lead the organization overall, with an increasing focus outward - on fundraising, partnerships, and community relationships. As New Art looks toward its 50th year and beyond, you are a vital part of that forward motion. 

Above all, this is a trusted-advisor and internal leadership role for someone who wants to help shape New Art’s next chapter - translating organizational vision into results, building strong and accountable teams, and creating an internal operation that runs with excellence and heart. 

To Apply

Please submit a resume and a cover letter - we’d especially like to hear, in your own voice, what draws you to the New Art Center and why this opportunity speaks to you. We are looking to fill this position as soon as possible and encourage early applications.

Please email all application materials to
jobs@newartcenter.org with the subject heading: [Name], Dir of Ops and Programs Applicant

New Art Center is a nonprofit visual arts organization in Newton, MA, offering classes, exhibitions, and community programs for artists of all ages and experience levels. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and encourage people of all backgrounds and abilities to apply.

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

Holyoke Media, Inc. | Holyoke, Massachusetts
Full-Time, Exempt | Nonprofit · Community Media | $68,000–$75,000/year, commensurate with experience

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

Holyoke Media, Inc. invites collaborative, community-minded leaders to explore the opportunity to serve as its next Executive Director — a meaningful opportunity to lead an independent 501(c)(3) community media organization serving the City of Holyoke, Massachusetts, and its approximately 40,000 residents.
From its studio and offices in downtown Holyoke, the Organization provides Public, Education, and Government (PEG) access programming — including government meeting coverage, community news, podcasts, and arts programming — along with production training and studio access for local residents, students, and organizations.
Our mission:
To create an open forum that enables and encourages the exchange of ideas, information, and culture across the City of Holyoke.

ORGANIZATION AT A GLANCE

• Residents served: 40,000+
• Established: 2007
• Annual budget: $840K
• Net asset base: $2.7M

THE MANDATE

Lead Holyoke Media through its next chapter — a new state-of-the-art studio, a renewed sponsorship and endowment strategy, and a community-informed strategic plan. Reporting to a nine-member working Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as Chief Executive of the Organization — the public face and principal spokesperson for Holyoke Media in the community, with partners, and with the media.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The role centers on five areas of responsibility:
Strategic Leadership & Board Partnership
Serve as chief executive, providing vision, direction, and day-to-day leadership. Partner closely with the working Board to develop and implement a new strategic plan informed by community feedback.
External Relations & Community Partnerships
Act as Holyoke Media's principal spokesperson and "connector," building collaborative partnerships across local government, higher education, public schools, and grassroots community organizations.
Fundraising, Development & Marketing
Build and grow the donor base; design and lead fundraising campaigns spanning sponsorship, grants, and endowment support. Direct the Organization's grant writer and lead marketing and PR efforts.
Operations & Staff Leadership
Lead with a hands-off, empowering style that trusts staff to do their jobs. Recruit, train, and support a small team; conduct yearly performance reviews; and build strong relationships among the Board, staff, and partners.
Financial Oversight & Administration
Oversee organizational budgeting and financial planning alongside the Organization's accountant, including monthly reporting, ensuring Holyoke Media operates within budget guidelines and maintains sound, compliant administrative and facility operations.

THE QUALIFIED CANDIDATE

Holyoke Media seeks a collaborative, community-oriented, and relationship-driven leader who is passionate about local media and the vital role it plays in public life. Specific requirements include:

Exceptional leadership, management, and organizational skills, including experience overseeing staff, budgets, and vendor relationships.
Experience — or strong transferable skills — in fundraising, donor development, sponsorship, or grant oversight.
Demonstrated success building collaborative partnerships across government, education, and community-based organizations.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, with a background in marketing, PR, or public-facing communications.
Experience with financial oversight, budgeting, and monthly financial reporting, and with supervising staff.
Strong strategic-planning ability — formal or informal — with the capacity to turn vision into an actionable plan.
An open-minded, flexible, easygoing approach to leadership that takes feedback well.
A bachelor's degree or equivalent in Communications, Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Marketing, Multimedia, or a related field; equivalent experience considered.
Bilingual/bicultural (Spanish/English) strongly preferred, reflecting the demographics of Holyoke; nonprofit board experience a plus.
A charismatic, entrepreneurial, and visionary approach to organizational growth and community engagement.

If you don't check off every box in the requirements listed above, you should still consider applying. Holyoke Media is dedicated to building an inclusive and equitable workplace that fosters a sense of belonging.

POSITION AT A GLANCE

• Salary range: $68,000–$75,000, commensurate with qualifications & experience
• Location: Holyoke, MA — statewide search across Western Mass., Berkshire County, Greater Boston, Northern CT, and Hampden/Hampshire counties
• Work model: Primarily on-site; remote flexibility Monday & Friday negotiable
• Reports to: Nine-member working Board of Directors
• Employment: Full-time, exempt; at-will
• Best consideration: Rolling review — early applications encouraged

ABOUT THE MH GROUP

This search is conducted by The MH Group on behalf of Holyoke Media, Inc. The MH Group LLC is a certified WBE and MBE nationwide executive search, workforce strategy, and advisory firm that partners with organizations to identify, attract, and recruit exceptional leaders who drive long-term success, strengthen culture, and accelerate strategic growth.
